title: AI builds my assets. I direct every one of them.
author: thezirHaze
selftext:
Solo dev on LittleBigFoot, a cozy stealth adventure. Just turned my blockout park into an actual forest, and the pipeline is probably the interesting part for this sub.

**AI doesn't make my models. It writes the code that builds them.** I generate a reference sheet, decide what's right about it and what isn't, then AI writes a Python script that builds the mesh in Blender to my spec. The script is the asset, so proportions stay editable and a family of nine trees stays a family. All 1,284 trees in the park came out of nine of those scripts.

**This is not a prompt-to-scene pipeline, and the difference is where the time goes.** Every asset is authored against a spec I wrote: palette cells it's allowed to sample, a triangle budget, a real-world height in metres, proportions checked against my character's 2.4 m. Generation is the fast part. Decisions and checks are the whole job.

Two examples of that actually biting:

I used a Meshy base body for my main character, then scored it against my own character sheet instead of trusting it. **It lost**, so the shipped body is a rebuild. Generative 3D is genuinely useful for organic shapes I can't script, and useless as a final asset. The only way to know which you're in is to measure.

And swapping the greybox trees for the real ones changed my pathfinding. Same positions, same heights, supposedly a pure art change. My main traversal walk went 286.3 m / 47.7 s to 295.5 m / 49.2 s, because the final trees carry real capsule colliders and the navmesh routes around them now.

**AI will produce an asset far faster than it will tell you the asset is wrong.** Most of my time goes into the checks, and the checks are why any of it ships.
